app.name: Bro or Fraud?
app.description: A fast, chaotic party-game collection for Indian Gen Z groups.

avoid: caste, religion, region, or accent-based jokes
pressuring players to disclose real secrets

gameModes.name: Pass the Bomb
coreLoop: Show a category or challenge.
The current player gives one valid answer aloud.
They pass the bomb before the hidden fuse expires.
Repeated or invalid answers cost a life.
The player holding the bomb when it explodes loses a life or takes a silly penalty.

roundModifiers.name: Reverse Direction
roundModifiers.description: Passing direction reverses after the next valid answer.

roundModifiers.name: Double Trouble
roundModifiers.description: Two bombs circulate; each holder must answer before passing.

roundModifiers.name: Alphabet Lock
roundModifiers.description: Every answer must start with the displayed letter.

roundModifiers.name: No Obvious Answers
roundModifiers.description: The group rejects the first predictable answer; use only with friendly consensus.

gameModes.name: Heads Up / Tilt
gameModes.tagline: You have the word. They have the clues.
coreLoop: Choose a content pack and round duration.
The guesser holds the phone against their forehead.
Teammates describe the word without saying it or a forbidden word.
Tilt down to mark correct and tilt up to skip; buttons are always available as fallback.
Show the final correct, skipped, and pass totals.

roundVariants.name: One Word Only
roundVariants.description: Clue-givers may say only one word per clue.

roundVariants.name: Forbidden Words
roundVariants.description: Each card includes one or two words the team cannot say.

roundVariants.name: Speed Blitz
roundVariants.description: The final 15 seconds award a bonus for consecutive correct answers.

gameModes.name: Confession Roulette
gameModes.tagline: Real answers. Fake answers. Who's bluffing?
coreLoop: Show a prompt to all players.
Each player privately submits a short answer or chooses a fictional answer.
Mix submissions with clearly marked system-generated decoys internally, but do not reveal which are decoys.
Reveal answers one at a time without authorship.
Players vote for the author or select Ghost/Decoy.
Reveal authorship and award points.

gameModes.name: Never Have I Ever
gameModes.tagline: Own it, deny it, or skip it.
coreLoop: Show one statement.
Each player privately chooses I Have, I Haven't, or Skip.
Reveal only aggregate counts by default.
If exactly one player chooses I Have and Detective Mode is enabled, the group can guess who it was.
Allow the player to decline any follow-up.

items.statement: Never have I ever posted a story mainly hoping one specific person would see it.
Never have I ever checked someone's profile so deeply that I reached content from a different era.
Never have I ever typed a reply, deleted it, rewritten it, and still sent 'lol'.
Never have I ever pretended not to care while tracking every tiny online signal.
Never have I ever opened an app automatically and forgotten why I opened it.
Never have I ever used a song on a story to communicate something I wouldn't say directly.
Never have I ever rehearsed how I'd act if I randomly met someone.
Never have I ever checked who viewed my story and built a whole theory from it.
Never have I ever kept a screenshot as evidence for a future argument that never happened.
Never have I ever said I was offline while actively scrolling.
Never have I ever saved a roadmap instead of starting the actual work.
Never have I ever added a tool to my resume because I understood one tutorial.
Never have I ever called a project 'almost done' when the main feature was still imaginary.
Never have I ever watched a productivity video to avoid doing the task.
Never have I ever opened a coding problem, read the examples, and immediately checked the solution.
Never have I ever joined a group project and discovered the group was just a WhatsApp notification.
Never have I ever said 'I'll start after this week' more than once.
Never have I ever used AI to explain an answer and then struggled to explain it myself.
Never have I ever made a timetable so ambitious that it failed before lunch.
Never have I ever presented a bug as a feature during a demo.

gameModes.name: Would You Rather
coreLoop: Show two mutually exclusive choices.
Players vote privately before seeing group results.
Reveal the vote split.
Optionally give one player from each side 20 seconds to defend the choice.
Award prediction points to players who correctly predict the majority.
